name: summaries
description: Four fictional sets of meeting notes and emails, written for testing. Each case asks for a short summary; its checklist says what a good summary must contain. Items that apply to every case are in config.json.

cases.input:
Summarise these notes for the chief executive in under 120 words.

Ops review, 3 November 2026. Present: Priya (ops), Tom (finance), Ana (IT).
- Warehouse B pick rate fell from 142 to 118 orders an hour in October after the new scanners. Ana says a firmware update fixes the lag; vendor ships it on 10 November.
- Overtime cost GBP 18,400 in October against a budget of GBP 9,000. Tom wants overtime capped from 1 December unless the pick rate recovers.
- Priya proposed hiring two temporary pickers until the fix is proven. Tom agreed for four weeks only.
- Decision: firmware update on 10 November, two temps from 7 November for four weeks, review on 8 December.

checklist: Says the pick rate fell after the new scanners
Mentions the firmware fix due on 10 November
States the overtime overspend (GBP 18,400 against GBP 9,000)
Gives the decision to hire two temporary pickers for four weeks

cases.input:
Summarise this email thread for the chief executive in under 120 words.

From Maria (legal), 28 October: Harbour Supplies want to raise prices 12% from January, citing freight costs. Our contract allows one increase a year capped at the consumer price index, currently 3.1%.
From Ken (purchasing), 29 October: They supply 40% of our furniture. Two alternative suppliers have quoted 6% and 9% above current prices.
From Maria, 30 October: We can refuse anything above 3.1%. If they insist, we may terminate on 90 days' notice.
From Ken, 31 October: Recommend we offer 3.1% and start a trial order with the 6% supplier as a fallback.

checklist: Says Harbour Supplies want a 12% increase from January
Explains the contract caps increases at the consumer price index (3.1%)
Gives the recommendation: offer 3.1% and trial the 6% supplier

cases.input:
Summarise these notes for the chief executive in under 120 words.

Security incident review, 4 November 2026.
- On 1 November a staff laptop was stolen from a car. The disk was encrypted and the device was wiped remotely within two hours.
- No customer data was stored on it; the user's email was synced, which held three supplier contracts.
- Legal says this is not a reportable breach because the disk was encrypted.
- Actions: remind staff not to leave devices in cars (HR, by 11 November); review which roles need email on laptops (IT, by 30 November).

checklist: Says a laptop was stolen and was encrypted and wiped
Says no customer data was on it
States that legal judged it not reportable
Lists both actions with their owners

cases.input:
Summarise this email for the chief executive in under 120 words.

From Sam (sales), 2 November: Q3 closed at GBP 2.41m against a target of GBP 2.6m, 7% short. The gap is almost entirely the Northwind renewal, which slipped to Q4 when their procurement head left; it is verbally agreed at GBP 210k. Excluding Northwind we beat target by 0.7%. Pipeline for Q4 is GBP 3.2m, of which GBP 1.1m is at contract stage. I'd like approval to offer Northwind a 5% discount for signing by 30 November.

checklist: Gives Q3 sales of GBP 2.41m against a GBP 2.6m target
Explains the shortfall is the Northwind renewal slipping to Q4
Mentions the Q4 pipeline of GBP 3.2m
States the request for approval of a 5% discount for signing by 30 November
